newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: BANK NEGARA MALAYSIA SELLS DOLLAR/RINGGIT -DEALERS.
newsitem.headline: BANK NEGARA MALAYSIA SELLS DOLLAR/RINGGIT -DEALERS.

text.p: Malaysia's central bank intervened in the foreign exchange market to sell the dollar in late afternoon trade to defend the ringgit following strong bids for the U.S. currency, dealers said.
The said Bank Negara sold the dollar/ringgit through an agent bank at 2.6500/10 at 0900 GMT.
"The selling was quite aggressive and I think they are still in the market offering dollar/ringgit," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.
No confirmation was available from Bank Negara, which does not normally comment on its open market operations.
Dealers said they were quite surprised over the central bank intervention as the dollar was not rising too fast.
"Probably Negara does not want the dollar to go above the recent high of 2.6530," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
At 0930 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6498/10 to a dollar, after hitting a high of 2.6520.
The ringgit remained under pressure after falling sharply overnight on rumours, later denied, that central bank governor Ahmad Mohamed Don had resigned.
Bank Negara's support of the ringgit followed Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's remark on Thursday that he was concerned with the sharp fall in the ringgit.
Dealers said dollar bids from offshore players as well as local corporates were evident throughout the day. This was met by some dollar sales by exporters around the 2.6500 level, they said.
Dealers said given the current weak fundamentals in Malaysia and bullish dollar sentiment, the ringgit could be heading for 2.70 against the dollar in the near term.
